statements.status_notes: CVE-2008-3234 says a remote authenticated user can obtain arbitrary SELinux roles in Debian's sshd by appending a role to the user name (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2008-3234). The behaviour comes from Debian's selinux-role patch, which lets a user name carry a requested SELinux role; OpenSSH upstream rejected that patch (https://bugzilla.mindrot.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1641) and Debian, which added it for https://bugs.debian.org/394795, still carries it in openssh 1:10.0p1-7+deb13u4. Debian lists it as unfixed and unimportant, with the note "this is by design". The DHI Debian repository publishes three builds of openssh for Debian 13, all rebuilds of Debian's 1:10.0p1-7+deb13u4. We checked the openssh-server packages of all three on amd64 and arm64, verified against the index checksums: sshd, sshd-session and sshd-auth all link libselinux.so.1 and import get_default_context_with_rolelevel, and sshd-session and sshd-auth contain the patch's role handling (mm_inform_authrole), so the code is present. Pending: a primary maintainer statement of why role selection is by design (the role is passed to libselinux, which should only grant a role the SELinux policy allows for that user), and a check on an SELinux-enforcing host that a user cannot get a role the policy does not allow.
